subject: ai
question: Explain backtracking search and constraint propagation in CSP.
title: Backtracking Meets Propagation
hook: What if a solver could undo its own mistakes?
answer: Backtracking search = depth-first search that assigns one variable at a time, checks the constraints, and undoes (backtracks) the last choice when a constraint is violated
Example (map colouring, D fixed to blue): A=red, B=green, C=blue then D clashes with C, so back up to B=blue, C=green, D=blue works

Constraint propagation = use the constraints to remove inconsistent values from the variables' domains before and during the search, e.g. arc consistency: every value needs a supporting partner in the neighbour's domain
Example: D={blue} and C touches D, so remove blue from C; then A=red leaves C={green} and B={blue}: solved with no backtracking
Combined: backtracking picks a value, propagation cleans the domains; an empty domain means back up at once
Memory trick: backtracking = try, check, undo; propagation = cross out first
